metadata.note: deep-explainer sourced from ai1-cli/chapters/09-convert-what-survives.md (a 'hard chapter' per the book's own spec, read in full, cross-checked against research/09-*.md). 4 acts: I the four conversion maps + the FTC legal edge stated once, II directing (not delegating) two conversions, III the real three-way worked example (original -> live agent conversion -> deliberately-blank human rewrite) + GATE 3 as the one agent-can-never-sign gate, IV the chapter's own what-can-go-wrong table + the bridge to ch10. The agent-conversion sentence in A3-2 is the chapter's own real, live transformation (not fabricated) -- the human-rewrite slot is honestly left blank per the chapter's own stated reasoning (faking one would be the exact dishonesty the chapter exists to prevent), and this video's narration preserves that honesty rather than inventing a fake rewrite. No Manim on this machine (pangocairo not installed) -- MANIM lane absorbed into REMOTION. VOX quota: 4 real Wikimedia Commons photographs (14.3% of 28 body beats, slightly under the usual 15-30% band -- several candidate images for this topic were rejected during sourcing: one turned out to be vulgar graffiti, one depicted an identifiable named individual, several searches hit Commons rate limits or returned no usable photographs -- a weak fifth image was not forced in to hit the quota exactly). BinaryBranch/DivergentFates hero beats planned up front at A1-5, A2-4, A3-4, A4-4 (one per act) for clean 9:16 Short derivation. Signed for Divyank from authoring time, including the outro card. GATE P: PENDING, see PEDAGOGY.md.

beats.narration_text: Hallo — this is Liam, in for Divyank. An agent can convert a profile into a case study in one clean pass — genre-correct, structurally right, and still not yours. This chapter is about the one signature no agent is ever allowed to give, and what it actually takes to earn it.

beats.act: Act I — Genre Transformation Isn't Freehand
beats.narration_text: Four maps, because the underlying skill transfers. Profile becomes customer case study. Proposal becomes sales page. Evaluation becomes product review. Rhetorical analysis becomes ad teardown.

beats.narration_text: Take the profile. It keeps the interview, the concrete detail — the underlying skill. What copywriting adds is a transformation arc, and a section that actually proves the result.

beats.act: Act III — The Human Rewrite, and the Signature No Agent Can Give
beats.narration_text: A signature carries a specific kind of weight a printed name never does — it's a person putting themselves behind the words, in a way that can't be delegated back out.

beats.narration_text: The original: 'a profile is an interview-based portrait of a person.' The agent conversion, produced live and real: 'a customer case study is an interview-based portrait of a buyer's transformation, rich with the proof that makes the outcome believable.' The map did its work.

beats.act: Act III — The Human Rewrite, and the Signature No Agent Can Give
beats.narration_text: The third column — the human rewrite — is deliberately left blank. The agent can convert the genre. It cannot supply your judgment about which result matters, which detail earns trust, or how much proof your reader needs.

beats.act: Act III — The Human Rewrite, and the Signature No Agent Can Give
beats.narration_text: The test is simple and unforgiving: read the rewrite aloud. If it still sounds like the internet, keep going. If it sounds like you, you're done.

beats.narration_text: GATE three, stated plainly: the author sign-off, the one gate in the entire system no agent may ever sign. A human read this and rewrote it into their own voice and judgment.

beats.narration_text: A mark means something specific, only when it's applied honestly — stamped on what actually earned it, and withheld from what didn't. Apply it to everything, and it stops meaning anything at all.

beats.act: Act IV — What Can Go Wrong
beats.narration_text: The conversion is generic — that means you let the agent drive. The fix is to re-direct: name the map, the reader, the specific proof. Conversion is directed, not requested.

beats.act: Act IV — What Can Go Wrong
beats.narration_text: A case study makes claims with no proof — the proof beat got skipped, and if it's incentivized, that's possibly non-compliant too. Add verifiable proof, disclose it, or cut the claim.

beats.act: Act IV — What Can Go Wrong
beats.narration_text: A claim ships either way. Disclosed, or cut if it can't be verified — legal, and still persuasive. Left incentivized and undisclosed — a testimonial the FTC's own rules were written to catch.

beats.act: verdict
beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. Genre transformation isn't freehand — each composition genre maps onto a copywriting counterpart because the underlying skill transfers: profile to case study, proposal to sales page, evaluation to product review, rhetorical analysis to ad teardown. Direct the conversion, don't delegate it: name the map, the reader, and the specific proof — an undirected conversion is structurally right and means nothing. GATE three is the one signature no agent may ever give: a human has to actually rewrite the conversion until it carries their own voice and judgment, not just edit it in place. And proof that sells has to also be proof that's legal — the FTC's rules on incentivized and undisclosed reviews apply the moment a case study or review becomes a testimonial.
